cursor.description:
A pagination cursor returned by a previous call to this endpoint. Provide this cursor to retrieve the next set of events for your original query.

For more information, see [Pagination](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/build-basics/common-api-patterns/pagination).

limit.description:
The maximum number of events to return in a single page. The response might contain fewer events. The default value is 100, which is also the maximum allowed value.

For more information, see [Pagination](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/build-basics/common-api-patterns/pagination).

Default: 100

query.description: The filtering and sorting criteria for the search request. To retrieve additional pages using a cursor, you must use the original query.

created_at.description: Filter events by when they were created.

SearchEventsQuery.description: Contains query criteria for the search.

field.description:
Sort events by event types.
See [SearchEventsSortField](#type-searcheventssortfield) for possible values

order.description:
The order to use for sorting the events.
See [SortOrder](#type-sortorder) for possible values

x-enum-elements.name: DEFAULT
x-enum-elements.description: Use the default sort key. The default behavior is to sort events by when they were created (`created_at`).

SearchEventsSortField.description: Specifies the sort key for events returned from a search.

x-enum-elements.name: DESC
x-enum-elements.description: The results are returned in descending (e.g., newest-first or Z-A) order.

x-enum-elements.name: ASC
x-enum-elements.description: The results are returned in ascending (e.g., oldest-first or A-Z) order.

SortOrder.description: The order (e.g., chronological or alphabetical) in which results from a request are returned.

TimeRange.description:
Represents a generic time range. The start and end values are
represented in RFC 3339 format. Time ranges are customized to be
inclusive or exclusive based on the needs of a particular endpoint.
Refer to the relevant endpoint-specific documentation to determine
how time ranges are handled.

start_at.description:
A datetime value in RFC 3339 format indicating when the time range
starts.

end_at.description:
A datetime value in RFC 3339 format indicating when the time range
ends.
